title: Throughput Service Credit Matrix and Autoscale Interlock Specification
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define a deterministic, simulation-backed service credit matrix for Dedicated throughput guarantees and the autoscale interlock that binds crediting to fleet controls. Produce a spec, on-call playbook hooks, and sample contract language for legal that balances predictable customer credits with anti-abuse safeguards.
background: Customers on Dedicated capacity have requested simpler, deterministic crediting tied to observable degradation modes (e.g., degraded throughput from autoscale cooldowns, node cordoning, AZ failover). Existing playbooks focus on ad-hoc credits; we need a repeatable matrix that maps measured degradation windows to capped monthly credits and a clear interlock between autoscale actions and contract remediation.
proposal_summary: 1) Define a quantile-aware credit formula (p50/p95/p99 thresholds) that converts measured serve-rate shortfall minutes into proportional monthly credits. 2) Implement an autoscale interlock state machine that records autoscale-trigger context (request spike, node failure, zone outage) and classifies events for credit eligibility. 3) Expose an entitlement API and monthly simulation report for customers. 4) Provide sample contract paragraphs with notice, cure periods, and maximum caps.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document reviewed and approved by Legal and SRE
Credit computation implemented as a reproducible nightly job that can run simulations over arbitrary time windows
Autoscale interlock events are logged with classification, causal tags, and preserved for 90 days
Entitlement API returns computed credits and per-window event diagnostics for a tenant for the last billing cycle
Pilot completed with 3 existing Dedicated customers and pilot feedback collected
success_metrics: Reduction in SLA disputes: >50% fewer credit-related tickets compared to baseline
Stability of credits: simulated monthly credits deviate <5% from observed credits after two weeks of production telemetry
Time-to-resolution for credit disputes: median <= 3 business days
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: Finalize spec and contract language; legal & finance signoff
Week 2: Implement credit engine and entitlement API; instrument autoscale interlock logging
Week 3: Run replay/simulation on last 6 months of Dedicated telemetry; tune thresholds
Week 4: Run closed beta with 3 customers; collect feedback and iterate
Week 5: Bake into billing pipeline and enable for new Dedicated contracts; offer opt-in for existing customers
technical_requirements: Consume per-tenant throughput histograms (1s granularity) from runtime metrics pipeline
Event capture for autoscale actions must include: timestamp, reason, affected nodes, pre/post capacity, sequence-id
Store classification metadata (user-impacting, maintenance, external-incident) as indexed tags
Nightly batch job that computes credit liability given statement period, applies caps, and writes evidence bundle
API endpoint: GET /entitlements/{tenant}/credits?cycle={YYYY-MM} returning computed_credit and diagnostics URL
contract_text_snippets: Proposed clause (plain language): If Redwood fails to deliver the Committed Throughput for a billing window, Customer is eligible to receive a Service Credit computed as described in the Throughput Credit Matrix. Credits are capped at 15% of that billing month's Dedicated capacity fee. To qualify, Customer must submit a claim within 30 days of the end of the affected billing window.

Proposed clause (detailed): Throughput shortfall is measured per billing period by comparing delivered tokens-per-minute against the Committed Throughput profile. Each minute of degradation is weighted by severity bucket (Minor, Major, Severe) and multiplied by the Tenant's monthly committed spend fraction to produce a proportional credit. Events caused by Customer configuration, scheduled maintenance with >=72h notice, or third-party cloud provider outages are excluded.

Notice and cure: Redwood will notify affected customers for major degradations within 4 hours of incident detection. Customers may opt to accept a remediation plan in lieu of immediate credit; such acceptance pauses credit accrual for the affected window. Legal review required for final phrasing.
monitoring_and_alerting: SLA metric dashboards: per-tenant p50/p95/p99 throughput vs committed baseline
Alert: tenant_throughput_shortfall_rate > 5% for 15m triggers paging to SRE
Alert: autoscale_interlock_classified_event created with classification=UserImpacting triggers investigation
Daily job health check: credit-engine-run-success metric should be true; failure creates billing-blocker ticket
open_questions: What is final numeric cap on monthly credits (finance prefers 10-15%)?
Do we allow retroactive adjustments beyond 60 days with mutual agreement?
How should we treat multi-region Dedicated pools with partial AZ impact? Pro-rate by served capacity or by tenant request routing?
What threshold of evidence is required for a customer dispute to override automated credit computation?
dependencies: ENG-50291 (metrics pipeline retention and per-tenant histograms)
ENG-50900 (autoscale event capture and state machine work)
LEGAL-1124 (contract language review and regulatory compliance)
BILLING-204 (billing pipeline support for credit application)
risks: Overly generous cap leads to outsized financial exposure on a high-volume tenant
Insufficient telemetry granularity causes contested credit computations
Autoscale interlock misclassification could incorrectly exclude eligible credits
Billing pipeline changes may delay credit application and frustrate customers
notes: Reference: competitor contract language examples collected in /legal/sla-examples
